claim: In autonomous scientific discovery, the reward signal is highly sparse because a true discovery can take years and the outcome of a single experiment does not serve as an effective reward signal.
falsifier: One could measure the frequency and informativeness of reward signals in a simulated scientific discovery environment and verify that most experiments yield no clear reward.

conditions: in the context of autonomous scientific discovery
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported review summary and the referenced works; transfer beyond the described setting is unestablished.

title: Nature of scientific discovery–sparse reward signal boundary

claim: Under the VPP schedule, peak reserved device memory reaches 51.7–54.6 GB per NPU, leaving a narrow margin from the per-device HBM budget; the additional residency demanded by DualPipeV (doubling resident parameters and gradients and larger in-flight activations) would overshoot this limit, forcing a smaller micro-batch size or heavier recomputation that erodes its efficiency gains.
falsifier: On a system with the same HBM budget and VPP schedule, measure peak memory usage with and without DualPipeV to verify whether memory overshoot occurs.

conditions: peak reserved device memory 51.7–54.6 GB per NPU
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported NPU system, VPP schedule, and profiled ranks; transfer beyond these conditions is unestablished.

title: DualPipeV's additional residency–overshoot of per-device HBM boundary
